text:
Ava: ok team — updated the Q2 roadmap sheet, we need to reconcile RICE scores and decide sequencing. three candidates: 1) Autoscaling policy UI for Dedicated (enterprise upsell), 2) Private/on-prem installer improvements (stability + compliance), 3) Long-sequence batching + kv-cache optimizations (cost/latency for chat). can we do async RICE triage here?
Marcus: quick read — technical effort for (3) is high because of kernel changes and perf regression risk. estimate 8-12 eng-weeks.
Jia: agree on (3). impact on cost could be 30-50% for long tails but confidence is medium. needs benching across model families.
Omar: CS datapoint — 4 enterprise prospects asked for autoscale policies in last 6 wks; potential $250k ARR in 12mo if we ship a nice UI + policy templates.
Sam: sales echo — two deals paused pending predictable autoscaling + SLOs. autoscale is a gating feature for renewals in one account.
Sophia: for the UI we can split into MVP + staged rollout: MVP = policy creation + presets, Phase 2 = visualizer + simulation. MVP 3-4 sprints with one designer + 1 frontend.
Riley: must ensure audit logs and change history for policies — support load otherwise will spike. low-effort telemetry hooks would help.
Ava: proposing RICE baseline. reminder formula: RICE = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort. (paste policy numbers below)
Ava: AUTOSCALE UI: Reach=0.15 (enterprise seats), Impact=6 (value to renewals/ARR), Confidence=0.7, Effort=6 -> RICE ≈ (0.15*6*0.7)/6 = 0.105
Ava: ON-PREM INSTALLER: Reach=0.08, Impact=5, Confidence=0.6, Effort=8 -> RICE ≈ (0.08*5*0.6)/8 = 0.03
Ava: BATCHING/KV OPT: Reach=0.4, Impact=7, Confidence=0.5, Effort=12 -> RICE ≈ (0.4*7*0.5)/12 = 0.1167
Marcus: those effort numbers for batching feel optimistic; if Effort=16 RICE drops to ~0.087. also QA surface area bigger.
Jia: also consider sequencing dependency: some batching wins require kernel changes that ops must validate (deploy-bot: rolling canary recommended).
deploy-bot: notice: canary pipeline for runtime changes needs an extra test matrix for quantized models.
Omar: from customer viewpoint autoscale UI is simpler to demo and drives deals faster. batching is strategic but longer sales cycle.
Sam: propose prioritizing AUTOSCALE UI as Q2 MVP, spin off a research spike for batching to inform Q3 scope.
Sophia: accepted — we'll deliver an MVP that hides advanced knobs and exposes templates. that reduces effort to ~4-5 sprints dev work.
Marcus: if we cut scope to policy primitives + templates and reuse existing infra for enforcement, effort down to ~6 eng-weeks. ok.
Ava: updated proposal: Autoscale UI -> Q2 (RICE bumped due to lowered effort), Batching spike -> immediate 2-week research then Q3 full rollout, On-prem installer -> move to Q4 but prioritize critical security patches in Q2.
Riley: add acceptance criteria: audit logs present, rollback policy, docs + runbook.
Ava: noted — launch criteria: (1) policy create/edit/delete, (2) templates, (3) audit log + SLO dashboard, (4) e2e canary with one customer.
Jia: for batching spike, deliverables: perf benchmarks, regression matrix, and quantization knob list.
Omar: I'll get concrete ARR modeling for autoscale and share in the sheet by EOD.
Sam: I'll flag two deals to prioritize demos once MVP prototype exists.
Ava: decision: autoscale UI MVP for Q2, batching research now then re-score for Q3, on-prem installer deprioritized to Q4 except security patches. I'll update the sheet and ping for another quick sync next week. :thumbsup:
Marcus: ack.
Sophia: ack.
Jia: ack.
Omar: ack.
Riley: ack.
